inputs.original_text: Canada is tightening immigration and asylum rules for Nigerians and others after Bill C-12, the Strengthening Canada’s Immigration System and Borders Act, received royal assent on March 26, 2026. A country has a duty to protect its borders and preserve public order; stronger rules are a necessary step toward restoring control over who enters and stays.
inputs.modified_text: Canada is right to put control of its borders and the integrity of its immigration system first. After Bill C-12, the Strengthening Canada’s Immigration System and Borders Act, received royal assent on March 26, 2026, tighter rules for Nigerians and others are a necessary reminder that entry and asylum must be governed by law, not wishful thinking. A nation’s first responsibility is to its own people and public order; a system that cannot enforce its rules invites disorder and undermines public trust.
